title: R’ Abba bar Yosef
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Beitzah, chapter 1, halakhah 3: R’ Yose son of R’ Bun said that R’ Zeira [ר״ז] and R’ Abba bar Yosef disagreed. Hyman identifies him as Rava, citing Beitzah 8b, and says he is mentioned under this name only once. Hyman explains this by saying that R’ Yose son of R’ Bun went down to Babylonia for a short time and, when he returned, brought this halakhah with him in Rava’s name; see his entry. We also find R’ Abba bar Yosef in Yalkut, Samuel I, remez 77, but the statement appears in Midrash Shmuel 1:7 in the name of R’ Abba bar Marya, in the name of R’ Yitzchak. Hyman calls the Sanhedrin, chapter 4, halakhah 8 reading, “R’ Abba bar Yasa in the name of R’ Yohanan,” a scribal error and says it should read as the statement appears there in chapter 1 [supplied label: ד״הד]: “R’ Abba, R’ Yasa, in the name of R’ Yohanan.” He explains that R’ Abba and R’ Yasa both said it in R’ Yohanan’s name.

notes.text: “Only once” belongs to Hyman’s argument about the name Abba bar Yosef. His Rava identification and reconstruction of the Abba/Yasa reporting chain remain his proposals. The Sanhedrin label ד״הד is retained as irregular.

All supplied personal titles are abbreviated here and remain R-prime, including Bun’s explicit father-title in both Yose son of Bun occurrences. Zeira is the contextual name interpretation of ר״ז, not newly verified full-title evidence. The chapter/halakhah citation format suggests Jerusalem Talmud, without a new exact passage check. Hyman’s Rava identification, only-once claim, brief journey to Babylonia and return with the teaching are his historical explanation, not an admitted identity or itinerary. Yalkut’s Abba bar Yosef and Midrash Shmuel’s Abba bar Marya remain separate reported forms. Hyman firmly says the Sanhedrin bar-Yasa reading is a scribal error and SHOULD READ the juxtaposed Abba/Yasa form; both co-reporters belong to his explicit explanation, not a freshly established chain. The supplied ד״הד stays unresolved. Prior bounded Venice chapter 1/4 nonmatches are not a global absence claim. All source holds remain.

Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah 1:3 names Abba bar Yosef in the dispute with Zeira. The consulted Bavli Beitzah 8b has alternative attributions to Yose bar Chama or Rava son of Rav Yosef bar Chama, with Zeira in both. The identity and journey are Hyman’s interpretation. Yalkut Shimoni on Samuel 77 names Abba bar Yosef in Yitzchak’s name, while the consulted Midrash Shmuel 1:7 reads Abba bar Madya. The consulted Hebrew Jerusalem Sanhedrin 4:8 reads Ba bar Yasa and 1:4 names Ba and Yasa separately in Yochanan’s name. Guggenheimer’s translation note on 4:8 also points to the separate reading.
